scope.included: Consumer and residential mortgage credit assessment by Italian banks and Article 106 intermediaries
assumptions: The borrower is a natural person acting as a consumer.
OpenCredit Evidence supports the assessment; the regulated lender remains the decision-maker.
AI and privacy obligations at EU level are handled by the EU baseline and Steel Thread controls.

eu_baseline: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), especially Annex III 5(b) and high-risk-system obligations
Directive 2008/48/EC and transition to Directive (EU) 2023/2225 (consumer credit)
EBA/GL/2020/06 on loan origination and monitoring
Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 (DORA), where the lender is in scope

platform_control_mapping.mi-1: data minimisation, egress controls, PII redaction and audit
platform_control_mapping.mi-4: model, call, latency, error, token, cost and sanitized audit evidence
platform_control_mapping.mi-11: human review, challenge, decision and feedback evidence

rules.title: Consumer creditworthiness assessment
rules.citation: D.Lgs. 385/1993 (TUB), Article 124-bis, current regime before the D.Lgs. 212/2025 adaptation deadline
rules.requirement_summary: Assess creditworthiness before concluding the agreement or materially increasing credit, using adequate information supplied by the consumer and, where necessary, an appropriate database.

evidence_requirements.description: Traceable rationale based on assessed facts

rules.title: Residential mortgage creditworthiness assessment
rules.requirement_summary: Perform a thorough assessment using necessary, sufficient and proportionate economic and financial information that is appropriately verified before concluding mortgage credit.

rules.title: Database information following consumer-credit refusal
rules.requirement_summary: Where refusal is based on consultation of a database, provide the consumer the required immediate and free information about the result and database consulted.

evidence_requirements.description: Evidence showing whether the database affected refusal

rules.title: Private credit-information systems safeguards
rules.citation: Garante decision no. 163 of 12 September 2019 and attached SIC Code of Conduct, Articles 3-14
rules.requirement_summary: Apply the national SIC rules on permitted purpose, notices, data quality, use, scoring, retention, security, rights and correction.

evidence_requirements.description: Database, query date and data provenance
Information about automated scoring where used

rules.title: Bank of Italy Central Credit Register instructions
rules.citation: Bank of Italy Circular no. 139 of 11 February 1991, as amended
rules.requirement_summary: Use, report and correct Central Credit Register information under the applicable instructions and preserve its reporting period and provenance.

rules.title: Transparency and fair customer relations
rules.citation: Bank of Italy provisions of 29 July 2009 on transparency, as amended
rules.requirement_summary: Maintain the required pre-contractual information, creditworthiness procedures, clear communications and complaints arrangements for the product.

rules.title: Bank governance and credit-risk controls
rules.citation: Bank of Italy Circular no. 285 of 17 December 2013, as amended
rules.requirement_summary: Place lending and outsourced technology within the bank's approved governance, internal-control and credit-risk framework.

rules.title: Article 106 intermediary governance and credit-risk controls
rules.citation: Bank of Italy Circular no. 288 of 3 April 2015, as amended
rules.requirement_summary: Place lending and outsourced technology within the intermediary's approved governance, internal-control and credit-risk framework.

rules.title: Italian personal-data protection overlay
rules.citation: D.Lgs. 196/2003, as amended, applied with the GDPR
rules.requirement_summary: Apply national safeguards, rights, remedies and enforcement provisions alongside GDPR duties for lending-data processing.

evidence_requirements.description: Record of purpose and lawful basis

rules.title: Customer due diligence and AML recordkeeping
rules.requirement_summary: Complete applicable customer due diligence, beneficial-owner checks, risk assessment and recordkeeping without exposing restricted AML information in AI evidence.

evidence_requirements.description: Restricted AML record reference, not its contents

rules.title: Time-specific anti-usury threshold check
rules.citation: Law no. 108 of 7 March 1996 and the applicable quarterly threshold decree
rules.requirement_summary: Check the financing's relevant rate and charges against the correct transaction category, amount band and quarterly threshold.

rules.title: Fair and non-misleading consumer communications
rules.requirement_summary: Keep marketing and consumer-facing explanations clear, accurate and free from unfair or misleading practices; do not reuse an internal AI summary as customer disclosure without review.

rules.title: Complaints and Banking and Financial Ombudsman route
rules.citation: Bank of Italy provisions on out-of-court banking and financial disputes, as amended
rules.requirement_summary: Preserve evidence needed for complaint investigation and provide the applicable complaint and ABF redress information.

rules.title: Italian AI principles and national governance
rules.citation: Law no. 132 of 23 September 2025, especially Articles 1-3
rules.requirement_summary: Apply Italy's human-centred, transparent, responsible, secure and non-discriminatory AI principles consistently with the EU AI Act.

evidence_requirements.description: EU AI Act and national-governance assessment

rules.transition_note: Contextual national overlay. Article 3(5) prevents this law from being treated as a separate new AI-system obligation beyond the EU AI Act.

rules.title: Upcoming consumer-credit data-source restrictions
rules.citation: D.Lgs. 212/2025 amendments to TUB Articles 124-bis and 125
rules.requirement_summary: Prepare to use necessary and proportionate verified economic and financial information and exclude special-category data and social-network data from creditworthiness assessment.
rules.transition_note: Non-blocking until 20 November 2026 or, if later, 90 days after the relevant Bank of Italy implementing provisions enter into force.

rules.title: Upcoming rights for automated creditworthiness processing
rules.requirement_summary: Prepare consumer notice, understandable explanation, expression-of-view and human-reconsideration routes for assessments based partly or wholly on automated processing.
rules.transition_note: Non-blocking until 20 November 2026 or, if later, 90 days after the relevant Bank of Italy implementing provisions enter into force.
